items.stem: Which Azure construct lets you apply Azure Policy and RBAC across several subscriptions at once?

options.rationale: Correct: management groups sit above subscriptions and pass policy and access down.
A resource group lives inside a single subscription.
Availability zones are datacenter groupings for resiliency, not governance scope.
A storage account holds data; it is not a governance scope.

items.explanation: Correct: management groups sit above subscriptions and pass policy and access down.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Azure resiliency are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Availability zones are physically separate locations within one Azure region
options.rationale: Correct: zones are separate locations inside a region.

options.text: Region pairs replicate across two regions for disaster recovery
options.rationale: Correct: region pairs provide cross-region resilience.

options.text: Availability zones protect against a whole-region outage
options.rationale: Zones are within a region; a region pair addresses regional loss.

options.text: Region pairs exist within a single datacenter
options.rationale: Region pairs span two regions, not one datacenter.

items.explanation: Correct: zones are separate locations inside a region.

items.stem: An event-driven task runs briefly and sporadically, and the team wants no servers to manage. Best compute choice?

options.rationale: Correct: Functions suit short, event-driven, serverless workloads.
An always-on VM wastes cost for sporadic work.
Scale sets manage many VMs; overkill for sporadic events.
This defeats the goal of no servers to manage.

items.explanation: Correct: Functions suit short, event-driven, serverless workloads.
